title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (inferred from the neighbouring pages). P is a regular n-gon with vertex set S and edge set A. Σ is the sphere obtained by doubling P, Σ* = Σ minus the n vertices, and P_ω is a base point. π_P = π_1(Σ*, P_ω) is free of rank n−1, generated by loops ρ_s (s ∈ S) around the punctures, subject to one product relation (59). D = D_P is the dihedral group of order 2n, and τ is the involution exchanging the two faces of Σ. π_P^{D,τ} ⊃ π_P^D are the orbifold ('extended') fundamental groups of Σ* under D×{1,τ} and under its orientation-preserving part D. The element ρ = ω̃ is the lift of the rotation, with ρ^n = 1. σ_a = σ̃_a τ_a is the order-2 lift attached to an edge a.

This page.
(76) ρ_s = ε_s², where ε_s = σ_{a_s} ρ. In particular ρ_0 = σ_{a0} ρ σ_{a0} ρ and ρ_1 = ρ ρ_0 ρ^{-1} = ρ σ_{a0} ρ σ_{a0}.
- Since ρ permutes the ρ_s cyclically by conjugation (73c), ρ and σ_{a0} generate π_P^D.
- (77) π_P^D ≅ ⟨ρ, σ_{a0} | ρ^n = σ_{a0}² = 1⟩ ≅ Z/n * Z/2. The relation (59) is a formal consequence of the two relations (78).
- Geometrically: Σ*/D is an orbifold sphere with one cone point of order n (the poles), one of order 2 (the edge-midpoint axes) and one puncture (the vertex-axis points, which become a cusp). So π_P^D is the Hecke group H_n, i.e. the (2,n,∞) triangle group. For n = 3 this is PSL_2(Z), which explains the marginal NB about identifying notations for n = 3.
- ε_s is the parabolic (cusp) element. Its square is the vertex loop ρ_s because the vertex stabilizer has order 2.
- π_P is the kernel of the natural map Z/n*Z/2 → D_n. This kernel is torsion-free of index 2n, with rank 1 − 2n(1/n + 1/2 − 1) = n − 1, as it must be.

Automorphisms of π_P.
- (79) ρ(ε_s) = ε_{ρ(s)} and ρ(ρ_s) = ρ_{ρ(s)}.
- A struck-out first attempt at the σ̃_b action is replaced by a marginal correction: τ_a(ρ_s) = ρ_s^{-1} when s is incident to a.
- Then (80): τ_{a0}(ρ_0) = ρ_0^{-1}, τ_{a0}(ρ_1) = ρ_1^{-1}, and τ_{a0}(ρ_i) = (ρ_{i-1}⋯ρ_1)^{-1}(ρ_i^{-1}), using the notation x(y) = xyx^{-1}. This is the standard action of the real-structure involution ('complex conjugation') on the generators of π_1 of a punctured sphere with real punctures. It is rewritten using the cyclic relation; Grothendieck's marginal note warns that the cyclic product must 'start with ρ_i and end with ρ_{i+1}'.
- General transport-of-structure rule: g̃(ε_s) = (ε_{g°(s)})^{sg(g)} and g̃(ρ_s) = (ρ_{g°(s)})^{sg(g)} for g ∈ D_P, where sg(g) = ±1 according to orientation.
- A marginal NB describes the action of τ_a as the composite of a change-of-base-point map λ_a with π_1 of the symmetry.

Purpose. These are explicit presentations and automorphism formulas for the 'polygonal' genus-0 piece of the Teichmüller tower, i.e. P^1 minus the n-th roots of unity with its dihedral symmetry. The next page completes the picture with π_P^{D,τ} ≅ (Z/n*Z/2) ⋊ Z/2, an extended Hecke group.
errors: The formula in (80) for τ_{a0}(ρ_i) was visibly being corrected: the second form '(ρ_i⋯ρ_{i+1})(ρ_i^{-1})' and the note 'commence avec ρ_i, finis ρ_{i+1}' show the index ordering was unsettled. The margin also says τ_{a0} was written where τ_0 was meant ('j'ai écrit τ_{a0} au lieu de τ_0'). The (80) formulas should be read with that caveat.
The first version of (80), giving the σ̃_b action, was crossed out and flagged 'A rectifier'. The corrected σ̃ formulas appear on the next page as (82).

Consistency check: (59) follows from ρ^n = σ² = 1 only if the product relation is read in the order ρ_{n-1}⋯ρ_1ρ_0 = 1. This product equals ρ^{n-1}(ρ_0ρ^{-1})^nρ with (ρ_0ρ^{-1})^n = σρ^nσ = 1. The opposite ordering does not reduce to 1, so the claim depends on the convention for (59).

ideas.what: Orbifold fundamental group of the doubled regular n-gon (sphere minus n vertices) modulo its dihedral symmetry is Z/n * Z/2, with the vertex loops as squares of cusp elements
ideas.modern_name: Hecke group H_n = (2,n,∞) triangle group; π_1(P^1 − μ_n) as the kernel of H_n → D_n
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hecke (1936) for the groups; the orbifold interpretation is standard (Thurston-era orbifold theory)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses dihedral/regular-polygon structures and the n=3 / PSL_2(Z) link, but not this explicit computation (unsure)

ideas.what: Explicit action of the dihedral group and the real-structure involution τ on free generators ρ_s of π_1 of the punctured sphere (ρ_s ↦ ρ_{g(s)}^{±1}, and the conjugation formulas for τ)
ideas.modern_name: Action of complex conjugation / mapping-class symmetries on π_1(P^1 − {real points}); extended Hecke group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; appears in Ihara, Nakamura and others' work on Galois actions on π_1 of P^1 minus points

deep.surprise_reason: These are careful but standard computations: the Hecke group presentation Z/n*Z/2 and the action of symmetries on free generators. The specific polygonal/orbifold framing shows how Grothendieck set up the genus-0 'Teichmüller tower' bricks, but contains nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: The first numbered equation on the page is (76), not (75); the text later cites '(76) et (73 c)', and the previous page already uses (74)/(75).
The marginal NB at left reads roughly: 'NB Pour n=3, on identifie dans les notations de P_n avec celles de V(?) ... σ_{a0} ... notations de σ_{a0}' (partly illegible).
The circled marginal note reads 'A rectifier : τ_a(ρ_s) = ρ_s^{-1} si s ∈ S incident à a ∈ A'.
The left margin near (80) reads approximately: 'Attention : j'ai écrit τ_{a0} au lieu de τ_0, (80) ; pour n=3 les relations requises ... τ_{a0} et τ_0 ... pour τ_0 !'
The final displayed system is unnumbered; it is (81) (struck '(81)' visible), generalizing (79) to all g ∈ D_P with sign sg(g).
